note: Every change made because it was claimed to shorten the ETA. judge_on is set when the change lands, not when it is convenient. concurrent_changes is what else was in flight, so a later reader can tell a clean attribution from a confounded one.

predictions.claim: Replacing the 0.5% guessed reservation with a bound derived from real consumption frees discretionary budget, so more laps fit in the same week.
predictions.metric: discretionary_percent reported by scripts/pacing.mjs, and laps per day in state/laps.json

min_observations.why: laps per day cannot be read off a pile of laps whose cost could not be measured. Six consecutive samples came back unusable, so a calendar date would have forced a verdict with no evidence under it.

predictions.deadline_reason: if three usable samples have not appeared by then, the method itself is the finding — say so and stop waiting for it.

predictions.claim: The registry listed revenue-loop as enabled after the owner stopped it, so the gate reserved quota for a trigger that cannot fire. Marking it disabled returns that share.
Ranking efficiency last while every path is infinite stops the loop spending laps on acceleration, so the next laps pick a candidate that could make a path finite.
predictions.metric: the kind of candidate chosen by each lap, read from state/continue.json and commit subjects

predictions.claim: Every candidate was a build act and none was a distribution act, while all three outside refutations landed on distribution. Adding findable_surface_at_scale and stopping discredited estimates from outranking honest blanks should change which candidate a lap actually executes.
predictions.metric: state/continue.json / state/laps.json show the next lap that selects work choosing a distribution-class candidate (findable_surface_at_scale, or the itch page judged on being found and referred) rather than a fifth build candidate. Falsified if laps keep selecting build candidates or machinery while the reranking sits unread.
concurrent_changes: codex INBOX task 2026-08-09.h aims the outside survey at the new candidate, so a refutation may arrive before the judge date and settle it the other way
predictions.note: The candidate deliberately carries no days-to-first-yen. Judging this on a day count would reproduce the exact error the change corrects, so it is judged on what gets executed.

predictions.claim: distribution_answer decided the itch.io page is judged on being found and referred rather than on existing, and wrote that decision only into zerobase.json. The itch candidate in eta.json — the file work is picked from — still read 'turns an infinite path finite' with no success test. Carrying the repricing onto the candidate should mean that when the owner action is spent, the lap that follows measures whether anyone found the page, instead of recording the page as done.
predictions.metric: after the itch page exists, whether the lap that handles it cites the success test (found and referred, or arrival from itch search/browse, from state/itch.json views) rather than the page's existence. Also whether eta.json keeps carrying success_test on the itch candidate across bot recomputes.
concurrent_changes: 2026-08-09.distribution-class-added — pushed by the other worker on this chain eight minutes earlier, from the same evidence. It reranked the candidates; this one only attaches a judging criterion, so the two are separable, but a reader should know both landed the same hour.
predictions.falsified_if: the page is created and the following lap records it as done without asking whether anyone found it, or the repricing stops reaching the candidate because reprices_candidates was dropped from zerobase.json

predictions.claim: high_intent_tool_site and npm_pypi_cli_pro will both fail the outside survey, and fail on the same term the previous five failed on: no case where the first buyer arrived from search or a listing unattended, with both calendar dates. Stated before the answer arrives so the loop's model of itself is testable rather than fitted afterwards. If it holds, all seven zero-base options are refuted and the round that produced them stops being a source of plans — that is the decision it forces, and it should be taken rather than answered with an eighth candidate.
predictions.metric: codex/outbox/2026-08-09.j.md, read directly. Confirmed if both candidates get 'なし' on the question of whether a first buyer arrived from search or a listing unattended. Partly confirmed if one does.
concurrent_changes: 2026-08-09.i landed the same hour and moved honest_post_where_buyers_gather from #4 to #7, which is what promoted these two to the top of the actionable list
predictions.falsified_if: either candidate produces a case with both calendar dates where the first buyer arrived from search or a listing with no simultaneous post, referral or existing following. One such case is enough to falsify this and it becomes the plan.

outcome.judged_early_because: judge_on was 2026-08-10, but the metric is codex/outbox/2026-08-09.j.md read directly, and it landed. Waiting for the date would have added nothing except a chance of nobody reading it — which is the failure this chain already made once with 2026-08-09.g.md.
outcome.measured: Both candidates returned なし on the question of whether a first buyer ever arrived from search or a listing unattended, and the survey marked both 落ちる.
outcome.result: CONFIRMED, in the strong form. The prediction allowed a partial pass if only one fell; both fell, and on the stated term rather than on some other weakness.
outcome.what_it_forces: The prediction stated its own consequence in advance: if it held, all seven zero-base options are refuted and the round stops being a source of plans, and that decision should be taken rather than answered with an eighth candidate. All seven are now refuted. The decision was taken this hour and is recorded as state/constraints.json no_standing_where_buyers_gather plus state/zerobase.json all_options_refuted.
outcome.attribution: Clean. The metric is a single external document produced before this lap read it, and nothing this loop did could change what it contained. This is the one prediction on the page whose confounders do not matter.
outcome.what_it_does_not_establish: That these products are unsellable. Monetisation was confirmed for five of the seven. Only unattended first-buyer arrival fell — and for npm_pypi_cli_pro the survey found no matching case in either direction, which is weaker than a refutation and is recorded as such on the option.

predictions.claim: The loop ranked by ETA and never once observed the ETA move. planned_eta existed only in a comment, there was no history, and none of the six predictions was measured in ETA units. With both numbers emitted and an append-only history, a later lap can finally answer whether anything shortened the goal — and the honest first answer may well be no.
predictions.metric: state/eta-history.json gains a row whose idle_eta_days or planned_eta_days differs from the row before it. Falsified if the history is still a single unchanged row: that would mean every change since was machinery, and the objective function never moved.

min_observations.why: one row is a baseline, not a trend. Two distinct rows is the minimum that can show movement at all.

predictions.deadline_reason: if the history still holds one row on 16 Aug, that is the finding: a week of laps moved no number that the goal is defined in. Say so plainly rather than waiting for a better week.
concurrent_changes: the chain restart at 10:59 changed who runs laps, so lap throughput is not constant across this window
predictions.note: null is the correct value for 'never' and the sanitizer now refuses a coerced number in the history. A row showing infinity becoming finite must be a real change, not a rounding.

predictions.claim: Route 1 was excluded on the wrong ground. The constraint written down was recurring owner actions; the blocker the evidence actually names is standing, which accrues before the post and is not a recurring action. Recording standing in state/constraints.json — where compute-eta.mjs reads it and turns it into a candidate — should change what laps do, because until now that exclusion lived only as prose in zerobase.json and no machine read it. The specific prediction: the constraint surfaces as an actionable candidate in state/eta.json and survives the scheduled bot recompute, and the next lap that selects work either picks it or states on the record why not.
predictions.metric: state/eta.json read back from origin/main: an entry with kind constraint_recheck and id no_standing_where_buyers_gather, actionable_now true, still present after a pulse/compute-eta run this session did not perform. Then state/continue.json and commit subjects for the following laps.
concurrent_changes: the parent applied a new eta-loop trigger prompt at 10:59 (ebb8cc0) making the parent a spawner rather than a worker. That changes who runs laps, so any change in what laps pick is confounded with it and cannot be attributed to this entry alone.

predictions.falsified_if: laps keep selecting build candidates or machinery without addressing standing or breadth, or the entry is dropped/rewritten by a later recompute so the picker stops seeing it. Also falsified if it surfaces but sits unread the way the zerobase repricing did — presence in the file is not the claim, being acted on or refused on the record is.
